title: Navruz: One New Year, Many Countries
intro: You are going to read about how people in different countries celebrate Navruz, the spring new year.

vocab.ex: We celebrate my grandfather's birthday every June.
Drinking green tea with guests is an old tradition in our family.
Close your eyes and make a wish!
Stir the soup slowly with a big spoon.

passage: On 20 or 21 March, the first day of spring, day and night are the same length. On this day, more than 300 million people celebrate the new year. The festival is called Navruz, which means "new day". It is an ancient holiday, more than 3,000 years old, and people in Central Asia, Iran, Azerbaijan and many other places still love it today.

In Uzbekistan, the most famous Navruz food is sumalak. Making it is hard work. First, women grow wheat in trays until it is green. Then they cook it with flour and oil in a giant pot. Someone has to stir it all night, so neighbours take turns. They sing songs, tell stories and laugh until the morning. There is also a fun tradition: people put small clean stones in the pot. If you find a stone in your bowl, you can make a wish.

In Iran, families decorate a special table called the haft-sin. They put seven things on it, and the name of each thing starts with the letter "s" in Persian. For example, there are apples, garlic and green wheat. Each thing is a symbol: apples mean beauty and garlic means good health. On the thirteenth day of the new year, most families leave the house and have a big picnic in a park.

In Azerbaijan, people jump over small fires in the weeks before Navruz. They believe the fire takes away the problems of the old year. Children also paint eggs in bright colours and play an egg game. Two players hit their eggs together, and the person with the unbroken egg wins. In Kazakhstan, people cook a soup called nauryz kozhe. It has seven ingredients, such as meat, milk and rice.

The food and games are different from country to country, but the main idea is the same. Navruz is a time to clean the house, buy new clothes and visit family. People share food with guests and forget old arguments. In 2009, UNESCO added Navruz to its list of important world traditions. After many centuries, this spring festival is still bringing people together.
